[LLOG.15.2] **A fact not asserted with the `logical` flag carries no TMS
justification link.** A `ttl` event, an `explicit` fact, an `activation`-scoped
fact ([LSCP.3]), or a synthetic `after`-timer fact (asserted plainly, [LTAC.3.3])
lives by its own declared lifecycle — TTL expiry, activation completion, explicit
retract, or one-shot timer firing — and the engine must not retract it on the
withdrawal of whatever asserted it. An `after`-timer's only cancellation channel is
`as`-keyed supersedure ([LTAC.2.2.1]), never justifier withdrawal.

The three surfaces that touch a derived or timer fact's justification lifecycle —
the `after`-timer, the `within`-window logical retract, and the event-trace order of
a truth-maintenance cascade against its trigger — are one principle, not three
behaviours: [LLOG.15.1] fixes what is truth-maintained, [LLOG.15.2] what is not.
